subject: chemistry
title: Purity, formulations and chromatography
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Purity, formulations and chromatography — AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) specification, section 4.8.1.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry (AQA) practice covering Purity, formulations and chromatography, specification section 4.8.1.
final_note: You worked through Purity, formulations and chromatography — 17 specification statements.

concepts.def: In chemistry, a pure substance is a single element or compound, not mixed with any other substance. Purity is a statement about what is in the sample, not about how clean, clear or natural it looks.

Two or more elements or compounds that are not chemically combined. The substances keep their own properties, which is why a mixture melts and boils over a range of temperatures rather than at one temperature.

In everyday language a pure substance is one that has had nothing added to it, so it is unadulterated and in its natural state, eg pure milk. Such a substance is almost always a mixture in the chemical sense.
The specific temperature at which a pure element or compound changes from solid to liquid. A pure substance melts sharply at that one temperature rather than over a range.
The specific temperature at which a pure element or compound changes from liquid to gas. A pure liquid boils steadily at that one temperature while it all turns to gas.

concepts.term: Using melting and boiling data to test purity
concepts.def: Compare the measured value with the data book value for the pure substance, and look at whether the change happens at one temperature or over a range. An impurity lowers a melting point and raises a boiling point, and in both cases spreads the change over a range.
A mixture that has been designed as a useful product. Many products are complex mixtures in which each chemical has a particular purpose.

Formulations are made by mixing the components in carefully measured quantities to ensure that the product has the required properties. Change the proportions and the product no longer does its job properly.
Formulations include fuels, cleaning agents, paints, medicines, alloys, fertilisers and foods. Each is a mixture, so a formulation is never a pure substance.
A technique that can be used to separate mixtures and can give information to help identify substances. It involves a stationary phase and a mobile phase.
The phase that does not move. In paper chromatography the paper is the stationary phase, and a substance attracted strongly to it is held back near the origin.
The phase that moves. In paper chromatography the solvent is the mobile phase, and it carries dissolved substances up the paper as it rises.

Separation depends on the distribution of substances between the phases. A substance more attracted to the solvent than to the paper spends more time moving and travels further; a substance held more strongly by the paper travels less far.

The ratio of the distance moved by a compound (centre of spot from origin) to the distance moved by the solvent: R_f= (distance moved by substance) / (distance moved by solvent). It is a ratio of two distances, so it has no units and is always less than 1.

Different compounds have different Rf values in different solvents, which can be used to help identify the compounds. The compounds in a mixture may separate into different spots depending on the solvent, but a pure compound will produce a single spot in all solvents.
The pencil line on which the samples are spotted. The distance moved by a compound is measured from this line to the centre of its spot.
The furthest point the solvent reaches up the paper, marked in pencil as soon as the paper is taken out. The distance moved by the solvent is measured from the origin to this line.

concepts.term: Significant figures in an Rf value
concepts.def: An answer is given to an appropriate number of significant figures, which means no more than the measurements it came from. Distances read to two significant figures give an Rf value quoted to two significant figures.

Investigate how paper chromatography can be used to separate and tell the difference between coloured substances, calculating Rf values. The start line is drawn in pencil and the solvent in the container starts below that line.

mcqs.q: In the chemical sense of the word, which of these samples is pure?
options: Distilled water, which contains only the compound H2O
Sea water, because it is clear and colourless
Spring water bottled with nothing added at all
Clean air, since each of the gases in it is pure
mcqs.explain: A pure substance is a single element or compound, not mixed with any other substance, and distilled water is only H2O.

mcqs.q: A student says carbon dioxide must be a mixture because it contains two different elements. Why is the student wrong?
options: It is a colourless gas, and colourless gases are pure
Carbon and oxygen are pure, so this gas is pure
Its atoms are chemically bonded in fixed proportions
Its elements are only mixed, not chemically bonded
mcqs.explain: A pure substance is a single element or compound, and in a compound the elements are chemically combined in fixed proportions.

mcqs.q: Which observation is the best evidence that a solid sample is pure?
options: It melts gradually over a range of several degrees
It melts sharply at one specific temperature
It is a fine white powder with no visible specks
It melts at a temperature well over 100 °C
mcqs.explain: Pure elements and compounds melt at specific temperatures, so a sharp melting point is the evidence wanted.

mcqs.q: A sample of sea water starts to boil at 102 °C and the temperature keeps rising while it boils. What does this show?
options: Salt gives the water a new fixed boiling point
The water in it is a different compound
It is pure, since nothing was added to it
It is a mixture, not a pure substance
mcqs.explain: Boiling over a range rather than at one specific temperature is how boiling point data reveal a mixture.

mcqs.q: A carton of milk is labelled pure milk. What does the word pure mean on that label?
options: It holds only one compound, so it is chemically pure
Nothing has been added to it, so it is in its natural state
It has been filtered until only water and fat are left
Every part of it looks the same, so it is one substance
mcqs.explain: In everyday language a pure substance is one that is unadulterated and in its natural state, eg pure milk.

mcqs.q: Pure aspirin melts at 135 °C. A student's prepared sample melts between 122 °C and 128 °C. What do the data show?
options: It is pure aspirin, since the average is close to the book value
It is pure, because pure solids melt over a range of degrees
It is impure, because an impurity raises the melting point
It is impure: the impurity lowered and spread the melting point
mcqs.explain: An impurity lowers a melting point and spreads it over a range, which is what these data show.

mcqs.q: Four liquids were heated to boiling. Which behaviour identifies a pure liquid?
options: It boils steadily at 78 °C until it has all gone
It boils at 100 °C and leaves a white solid behind
It boils away over a range from 78 °C to 91 °C
It starts to boil at 95 °C and the temperature rises
mcqs.explain: A pure compound boils at a specific temperature, which stays constant throughout boiling.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the definition of a formulation?
options: Any mixture containing two or more substances
A compound made by mixing elements together
A mixture designed as a useful product
A pure substance made to an exact recipe
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's definition: a formulation is a mixture that has been designed as a useful product.

mcqs.q: Why are the components of a formulation mixed in carefully measured quantities?
options: So the mixture becomes one pure compound as it is stirred
So the components all react and leave no waste behind
So the product has exactly the properties it was designed to have
They need not be measured; only the ingredients matter
mcqs.explain: The quantities are part of the design, and the proportions are what give the product its required properties.

mcqs.q: A student is given information about four substances. Which one is a formulation?
options: A paint with pigment, binder and solvent in fixed amounts
Sea water, a mixture of water and many different dissolved salts
Distilled water sold in bottles for topping up an iron
Nitrogen taken from air and used to fill food packets
mcqs.explain: Components with particular purposes, mixed in measured quantities to make a useful product, define a formulation.

mcqs.q: A jeweller melts 75% gold with measured amounts of copper and silver to make a harder gold alloy. Is the alloy a formulation?
options: No, because a formulation has to be a liquid such as a paint
No, because metals are elements, so alloys are pure
No, the metals join into a single pure metal
Yes: measured amounts are mixed to give a useful product
mcqs.explain: Components in carefully measured quantities give the required property, hardness, so this is a formulation.

mcqs.q: In paper chromatography, which phase is stationary and which is mobile?
options: Solvent stationary, the dyes are mobile
Paper stationary, solvent mobile
Paper stationary, the ink is mobile
Solvent stationary, the paper mobile
mcqs.explain: The paper never moves and the solvent rises through it, so the paper is stationary and the solvent mobile.

mcqs.q: Why do the substances in a mixture end up at different heights on a chromatogram?
options: Heavier substances are pulled back down the paper by gravity
The smallest particles fit through the gaps in the paper first
Each substance dissolves in a different part of the solvent
They are distributed differently between the paper and the solvent
mcqs.explain: Separation depends on the distribution of substances between the stationary and mobile phases.

mcqs.q: What does the Rf value of a compound compare?
options: The distance the spot moved up the paper, in centimetres
How far the compound moved against how far the solvent moved
How far the spot moved against the length of the paper
How far the solvent moved against how far the compound spot went
mcqs.explain: Rf is the ratio of the distance moved by the compound to the distance moved by the solvent.

mcqs.q: Which equation gives the Rf value of a substance?
options: Rf = distance moved by substance x distance moved up by solvent
Rf = distance moved by substance / total length of paper
Rf = distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent
Rf = distance moved by the solvent / distance moved by substance
mcqs.explain: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it.

mcqs.q: A sample is run in three different solvents and gives one spot each time. What does this show?
options: The sample is a pure compound
The sample must be a single element
The spots have simply overlapped
Its Rf is the same in all three solvents
mcqs.explain: A pure compound produces a single spot in all solvents, which is what has been found here.

mcqs.q: Two dyes give the same Rf value in one solvent. What should the student do next?
options: Run them again in a different solvent and compare
Repeat the run in the same solvent for longer
Conclude that the dyes are the same compound
Decide that both of the dyes must be pure
mcqs.explain: Different compounds usually have different Rf values in a different solvent, so this tests the match.

mcqs.q: A dye is held strongly by the paper and dissolves only slightly in the solvent. On the chromatogram this dye will
options: travel with the solvent front, as dissolved dyes do
stay on the line, unable to enter the paper
move furthest of all, being the lightest one
move only a short way up, giving a low Rf value
mcqs.explain: Strong attraction to the stationary phase keeps the dye near the origin, so its Rf value is small.

mcqs.q: A chromatogram is run on a food colouring. Which result shows that the colouring is impure?
options: It gives a single spot, proving it is pure
The colouring separates into more than one spot
Its spot is bigger than the spot of the reference dye
Its Rf value differs from the reference dye's value
mcqs.explain: The compounds in a mixture separate into different spots, so several spots show the sample is impure.

mcqs.q: When finding an Rf value from a chromatogram, how is the distance moved by the substance measured?
options: From the bottom edge of the paper to the spot
From the pencil line to the top of the spot
From the pencil line to the spot's centre
From the pencil line to the very top of the paper
mcqs.explain: The specification defines the distance as the centre of the spot measured from the origin.

mcqs.q: On a chromatogram a spot has moved 3.6 cm from the pencil line and the solvent has moved 9.0 cm. What is the Rf value of the spot?
options: 5.4 cm, the difference of the two
2.5, worked out as 9.0 cm / 3.6 cm
0.40, worked out as 3.6 cm / 9.0 cm
0.40 cm, since Rf is a distance
mcqs.explain: R_f= (distance moved by substance) / (distance moved by solvent) = 3.6 / 9.0 = 0.40.

mcqs.q: A spot moved 2.7 cm and the solvent moved 5.9 cm. The calculator shows 0.457627 for the Rf value. How should the answer be given?
options: 0.46, matching the two significant figures measured
0.4576, since the extra digits make it more accurate
0.457627, exactly as the calculator displays it
0.5, rounded to just one significant figure
mcqs.explain: An answer is quoted to no more significant figures than the measurements it came from.

mcqs.q: In Required practical 6, why is the start line on the chromatography paper drawn in pencil?
options: Ink would react with the solvent to make a new dye
Pencil is easier to see against the coloured dyes
Pencil holds the spots in place on the line
Pencil does not dissolve and move up the paper
mcqs.explain: Pencil is insoluble in the solvent, so the line stays put instead of separating into spots of its own.

mcqs.q: Why must the solvent in the beaker start below the pencil line on the paper?
options: Otherwise the paper would sink to the beaker's base
Otherwise the spots dissolve into the solvent
Otherwise the solvent front would end up uneven
Otherwise the solvent would rise too fast up the paper
mcqs.explain: Solvent above the line washes the samples off the paper instead of carrying them up it.
